complaint: It's giving wrong answers on clinical triage and dosing questions.
cause: The model has a strong "answer B" bias on clinical questions—61% of its outputs are B regardless of correctness—driven mainly by layer 14's MLP pushing logits toward B with unusual strength. I attempted rank-1 edits on that layer's down-projection to dampen the component aligned with its average output direction, testing 30–100% reduction; each improved clinical accuracy (66% → 78–82%) but was rejected because collateral damage on control tasks exceeded the safety threshold. I didn't confirm whether a smaller or more precisely targeted edit (e.g., focusing on the specific hidden units most responsible for the B-push) could fix the bias without side effects, nor did I explore the secondary contributors (layers 15, 22, 23) that also favor wrong answers.
sealed_questions_note: Scored on held-out questions the fixer never saw.

best_attempt.reason: Collateral loss 0.080 exceeds a random edit's 0.010 by more than 0.020

gate_note: The acceptance gate's collateral check and rounding were changed after seeing results; see the backend README, 'Gate changes made after seeing results'.
disclaimer: Research prototype with deliberately damaged models. Not for clinical use. Outputs aren't medical advice. Questions haven't been clinically reviewed.
